- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is below recent low, adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overestimating recovery.
- If forecast shows sharp spike followed by rapid decline, reduce peak value by 5–10% to account for overshoot.
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 3–5 days, apply a 1–3% upward bias to correct for mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope and add downward bias to avoid lagged sentiment misalignment.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates > 3% from forecast at day 1–3, apply a “first-day correction” rule: adjust day 1 forecast to match day 3–5 true trend.
